analysis:
The change in docs/architecture/inference.md is documentation-only. The head patch adds lines 716-749 describing an excluded shape warmup (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup) that runs synthetic probes and cells once per loaded engine, and a startup preload that warms each loaded model after any passing self-test and before registration. The supplied head excerpt (unit 9bceb6d953b336e2:7) starts at line 1 and was truncated around line 415, so the added lines 716-749 are not visible in the numbered text. The patch excerpt is also cut off mid-sentence. I could only evaluate the described behavior from the patch text, not the implementing source.

Security-relevant observations from the patch text: (1) The warmup uses provider-synthesized prompts with the artifact's default sampling, so it should not touch consumer prompts (A-001). The documented behavior says no probe or cell trains a rate or counter, which limits influence on routing or capacity evidence. (2) Warmup runs before registration, so routed traffic cannot preempt it. Preemption leaves the attempt due, so routed traffic still takes priority. A 20-second wall budget bounds the availability impact (T-010, T-029). (3) Whether warmup prompts could be donated to the SSD prefix cache (T-041) is not stated in the visible text. Synthetic prompts would carry no tenant data, but the cache-scope and donation behavior of warmup requests is a question for the implementing code, not something this docs diff shows. (4) No change to the threat-model-relevant boundaries TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 or TB-011 is claimed. The remainder of the unit (the base and head excerpts through line 415 and base lines 1622-1777) is unchanged context and adds no new claim of a security control.

No findings. The implementing source for the warmup was not supplied, so the contract is unverified. If a code pass sees shapeWarmup, it should confirm that warmup requests use no consumer data, do not publish prefix-cache or SSD donations under a real scope, and cannot delay LOAD/registration beyond the 20 s budget.
